settings.headline: Which injection are you booking?
settings.body: Both sub-procedures have their own collection — the recommended strength, the right format, and the products built for that kind of session.

settings.headline: Clinical Strength is the default.
settings.body: Most injection appointments are short, focused, and predictable in their demands. Clinical Strength cream is formulated for exactly that — top-ups, routine fillers, the appointments most clients book most often. If your session runs longer, covers a larger area, or you're prone to more sensitivity, Advanced sits one step up. Professional is rarely needed for injection prep — it's built for procedures that ask more of the skin than injectables typically do.

settings.headline: The products built for injection prep.
settings.body: Cream is the default for injection appointments. Spray suits sessions where injections are spread across a wider area.

settings.headline: Injection prep is its own thing.
settings.body: Injection appointments tend to run on tight windows. Booking, prep, session, recovery — often inside an hour. The cream needs to suit that pace. Senseless is formulated to fit how aesthetic injection appointments actually run, not how a generic skin cream wishes they did.
settings.image_alt: Editorial product close-up of Senseless cream

settings.headline: What comes next.
settings.body: Most aesthetic appointments end with a treated area that needs gentle handling. The Senseless Foaming Cleanser is built for the hours after. An antibacterial cleansing foam that respects what you just had done.
settings.image_alt: Editorial image of the Senseless Foaming Cleanser on a clean countertop

settings.question: Which strength should I choose for injections?
settings.answer: Clinical Strength suits most injection appointments — top-ups, routine fillers, Botox. Advanced for longer sessions or if you're prone to sensitivity. See choose your strength for the full breakdown.

settings.question: When do I apply it before my injection appointment?
settings.answer: Apply ahead of your appointment. The specific timing varies by procedure and how you respond to topical preparations — your practitioner is the best guide for the appointment you've booked.

settings.question: Can I use this for lip fillers specifically?
settings.answer: Yes — see our Lip Fillers collection for the focused recommendation.

settings.question: Can I use this for blood tests or vaccinations?
settings.answer: Senseless is formulated for aesthetic procedures. For medical injections, ask your healthcare provider for guidance specific to their practice.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product. Not a medicine. Not a pharmacy product.
